documents.text:
A sub-app's own [`ErrorHandler`](#errorhandler), `Views` and `ViewsLayout` still apply to the requests under its mount path, but only when the whole mount path, from the top-level app down, is literal. Under a parameter, as in `app.Use("/t/:tenant", tenantApp)`, the routes match and run while the nearest enclosing mount with a literal path, or the top-level app, supplies the error handler and the view engine. A [`Domain`](#domain) mount matches a parameterized path as a pattern, so its sub-app keeps its own. The [`RegexHandler`](./fiber.md#regexhandler) of a sub-app mounted on the top-level app compiles the `regex()` constraints in the full path of every route below it, the mount prefix included, so an app mounted deeper does not use its own.
:::

A sub-app mounted with `app.Use` can set its own `ErrorHandler`. It answers every error raised under the mount path, including the **404** for a path that matches none of the sub-app's routes. An app mounted inside it without a handler of its own uses it too, and any other request falls back to the parent's handler. This needs a literal mount path, taken from the top-level app down: the lookup compares the request path with the mount path as text, so under a parameter, as in `app.Use("/t/:tenant", tenantApp)`, the sub-app's routes still match and run but its handler is not found, and neither is the handler of an app mounted inside it. The handler of the nearest enclosing mount with a literal path answers instead, or the top-level app's handler when there is none. A sub-app mounted through [`Domain`](../api/app.md#domain) matches a parameterized mount path as a pattern and keeps its own handler.

Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
